paris/neighborhood-1.title: File:Abadía de Saint-Germain-des-Prés, París, Francia, 2022-11-01, DD 20-22 HDR.jpg
paris/neighborhood-1.author: Diego Delso
paris/neighborhood-1.description: Choir of the  Abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés , Paris, France. The church is located in the  Saint-Germain-des-Prés  quarter and was originally the church of a  Benedictine  abbey founded in 558 by Childebert I, the son of  Clovis , King of the Franks. It was destroyed by the  Vikings , rebuilt, and renamed in the 8th century for  Saint Germain , an early Bishop of the city.  it was rebuilt with elements in the new Gothic style in the eleventh century. It is considered the oldest existing church in Paris.

londres/region-list-1.title: File:Puente de la Torre, Londres, Inglaterra, 2014-08-11, DD 092.JPG
londres/region-list-1.author: Diego Delso
londres/region-list-1.description: The  Tower Bridge  is a  bascule  and  suspension bridge  located in the center of London that crosses the  River Thames . Its name is taken from the  Tower of London , located nearby and has become an iconic symbol of London. The bridge was built between 1886 and 1894 and has a length of 244 m (800 feet) and the height of the towers is 65 m (213 feet). The 61 m (200 feet) long central span is split into two equal bascules than can be raised 86 degrees to allow the transit of ships. Otherwise the bridge is open to the traffic and to the pedestrians.

istambul/day-0.author: Diego Delso
istambul/day-0.description: View of the  Basilica Cistern ,  Istanbul , Turkey. The Basilica Cistern, or Cisterna Basilica is the largest of several hundred ancient  cisterns  that lie beneath the city. This subterranean cistern was called Basilica because it was located under a large public square, the Stoa Basilica, on the  First Hill of Constantinople . fernando-de-noronha/attraction-5.description:
Praia da Atalaia, Fernando de Noronha. The natural pool with the people on the right is one of the island's main touristic attractions. 
Fernando de Noronha is an archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean, midway from South America to Africa, around 220 miles (354 km) away from the Brazilian coast. It is a special municipality (distrito estatal) of the Brazilian state of Pernambuco. (en:Fernando de Noronha)

sao-francisco/map-list-1.title: File:San Francisco (CA, USA), Alcatraz -- 2022 -- 3133.jpg
sao-francisco/map-list-1.author: Dietmar Rabich
sao-francisco/map-list-1.description: Stairs to Officers’ Row Garden, Alcatraz Island, San Francisco, California, USAAlcatraz, the rocky island in San Francisco Bay, transformed from a strategic military base to the most notorious maximum security prison in the United States. Originally designated as a military fort to secure the gold rush town in 1850, it later housed the army’s first military prison. Due to its isolated location and treacherous, freezing currents, the Department of Justice took over the island in 1934 and turned it into a federal prison.Here, under the strictest regime, serious criminals such as Al Capone and “Birdman” Robert Stroud were interned. The concept was simple: anyone who broke the rules ended up in Alcatraz – a place without privileges. Despite 14 escape attempts, the prison is officially considered escape-proof, even if the spectacular escape of 1962 still leaves questions unanswered today. In 1963, operations were discontinued due to high maintenance costs. Another important chapter in the prison’s history is its occupation by activists from the “Indians of All Tribes” (1969–1971), who used the island as a symbol for indigenous rights. Today, Alcatraz is part of the National Recreation Area and attracts millions of visitors annually as a museum.

sao-francisco/day-1.description:
Out of fog Bay Bridge and Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco in fog and w:crepuscular rays.  The image was sent to Dr. Andrew T. Young,. Here's his description: "... it's unusual to see these shadows so clearly at such an oblique geometry: usually, the crepuscular rays are best seen in forward scattering, and much less well in back-scattering.But here, you're looking almost at right angles to the illuminating rays."

montreal/map-attraction-2.title: File:Notre-Dame de Montréal Basilica 01.jpg
montreal/map-attraction-2.author: Wilfredor
montreal/map-attraction-2.description: The Sacré-Cœur Chapel of Notre-Dame Basilica was built from 1889 to 1891 according to the plans of the architects Henri-Maurice Perreault and Albert Ménard. Predominated by a neo-Gothic style, the chapel is typical of late-19th century architectural eclecticism and orientalization of architectural culture. It is characterized by the opulence of its woodwork and carved ornaments. The chapel was completely destroyed by a fire on December 7, 1978, except for one aisle and part of the rood screen. Jodoin Lamarre Pratte architects (then Jodoin Lamarre Pratte et associés, architectes) was mandated in December 1978 to rebuild the chapel. Mr. Denis Lamarre, architect and founding member of the firm, then suggested to rebuild the chapel partly according to the original plans and to modernize some elements, rather than performing a restoration entirely faithful to the original construction.

chicago/map-list-0.title: File:Millennium Park, Chicago, Illinois (9181711234).jpg
chicago/map-list-0.author: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA
chicago/map-list-0.description:
Millennium Park is a public park located in the Loop community area of Chicago in Illinois, USA and originally intended to celebrate the millennium. It is a prominent civic center near the city's Lake Michigan shoreline that covers a 24.5-acre (99,000 m2) section of northwestern Grant Park. The area was previously occupied by parkland, Illinois Central rail yards, and parking lots. The park, which is bounded by Michigan Avenue, Randolph Street, Columbus Drive and East Monroe Drive, features a variety of public art. As of 2009, Millennium Park trailed only Navy Pier as a Chicago tourist attraction.
Planning of the park began in October 1997. Construction began in October 1998, and Millennium Park was opened in a ceremony on July 16, 2004, four years behind schedule. The three-day opening celebrations were attended by some 300,000 people and included an inaugural concert by the Grant Park Orchestra and Chorus. The park has received awards for its accessibility and green design. Millennium Park has free admission, and features the Jay Pritzker Pavilion, Cloud Gate, the Crown Fountain, the Lurie Garden, and various other attractions. The park is connected by the BP Pedestrian Bridge and the Nichols Bridgeway to other parts of Grant Park. Because the park sits atop a parking garage and the commuter rail Millennium Station, it is considered the world's largest rooftop garden.

las-vegas/attraction-0.description: “The Strip” (part of the Las Vegas Boulevard) in Las Vegas, Nevada, USAThe Las Vegas Strip is the most famous section of Las Vegas Boulevard in Las Vegas. It stretches for around 6.8 kilometers south of downtown and is world-famous for its spectacular hotels, casinos, and neon signs.Its development began in the 1940s with the construction of large resort hotels such as the Flamingo Las Vegas. In the following decades, ever larger themed hotels were built, including the Bellagio with its famous water features and the Roman-style Caesars Palace. The Strip stands for entertainment in XXL format: casinos, shows, concerts, luxury shopping, and elaborate architecture characterize the scene. Many buildings feature international motifs – from Egyptian pyramids to the Eiffel Tower.Today, the Las Vegas Strip is one of the most visited tourist destinations in the USA and a symbol of glamour, gambling and night-time lights in the Nevada desert.

las-vegas/attraction-5.author: Dietmar Rabich
las-vegas/attraction-5.description: Intake towers of the Hoover Dam on the side of Nevada, Nevada/Arizona, USAThe Hoover Dam is a monumental dam on the Colorado River between the states of Nevada and Arizona. It was built between 1931 and 1936 during the Great Depression and was one of the largest construction projects of its time. Thousands of workers were involved; the construction was considered a technical masterpiece.The dam is named after President Herbert Hoover, who promoted the project politically. The enormous arch dam is around 221 meters high and consists of millions of cubic meters of concrete. It dams the Colorado River to form Lake Mead, one of the largest reservoirs in the USA.The aim of the project was flood control, irrigation, and power generation for the southwestern United States. To this day, the hydroelectric power plant supplies energy to millions of people. The Hoover Dam is considered a symbol of American engineering and economic prosperity.

boston/map-attraction-0.author: xiquinhosilva
boston/map-attraction-0.description:
The Freedom Trail in Boston is a 2.5-mile journey through history, connecting 16 nationally significant historic sites. It offers a rich narrative of the American Revolution, as each site stands as a testament to the courage and struggle for freedom that shaped the United States. 
From the iconic Boston Common to the USS Constitution, the trail brings to life the stories of the people and events that fought for America's independence. Walking this trail is like stepping back in time, providing a powerful and educational experience for visitors of all ages.

boston/day-1.title: File:Boston Common (7194230690).jpg
boston/day-1.author: InSapphoWeTrust from Los Angeles, California, USA
boston/day-1.description:
In the Boston area, urban planning often followed that of 17th Century England, where the settlers hailed from. Boston Common is one such feature; in English towns, a "common" is a common area of land that the residents could use on a communal basis for agricultural, grazing, and other uses. Boston Common has the distinction of being America's oldest urban park, dating back to 1634.

Boston Common is also the southern terminus of the Freedom Trail, which meanders through downtown to connect various historical points of interest. Its northern terminus is across the Charles River at Bunker Hill. The trail is marked with red bricks (as seen here) or with a red painted line.
